purpose: Classify the reciprocal radial average as a regularized discrete logarithmic-energy identity, identify the angular first variation as a conjugate-Poisson kernel, and preserve the moving-selector boundary.

classification.recommended_terminology: root-direction logarithmic-energy sweep with conjugate-Poisson angular first variation
nearest_prior_work: Lalin and Smyth (2013), Theorem 1 setup, uses the conjugate-reciprocal adjoint h*(z)=z^n overline{h}(1/z).
Garcia, Mashreghi, and Ross (2016), equation (1.1), gives the standard finite Blaschke-product factorization associated with disk zeros.
Katznelson, An Introduction to Harmonic Analysis, Section 2.6, equation (2.9), gives Q(r,theta)=2r sin(theta)/(1-2r cos(theta)+r^2) as the conjugate Poisson kernel.
classification.attribution: Attribute reciprocal adjoints, finite Blaschke products, positive Fourier kernels, and the conjugate Poisson kernel to standard complex and harmonic analysis. Credit the card only for the exact root-direction synthesis, its discrete-energy positivity law, and the explicit moving-selector boundary.
classification.mathematical_interest: The identity converts a geometric-mean estimate into a pointwise-in-radius existence statement and makes the selector instability visible at first order.
classification.reusable_scope: Equal-modulus point configurations on a circle, reciprocal-polynomial estimates, finite-Blaschke comparisons, and perturbative selector problems near a regular polygon.
classification.why_it_matters: It identifies exactly what averaging proves and what it cannot prove: existence at every radius survives, while a single spoke across all radii does not follow.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: The reciprocal logarithm has the Fourier expansion -log|1-w|=sum Re(w^m)/m, and the equal-modulus double sum has nonnegative Fourier coefficients |sigma_m|^2.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: Evaluate that kernel only on the polynomial's own root directions, combine it with the Blaschke majorant, and linearize the resulting selector functional near a regular polygon.
mechanism_comparison.quantifier_boundary: A nonpositive geometric mean at every radius yields for-all-t exists-j, not exists-j for-all-t. The separate exact one-spoke countermodel shows the latter is false.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The synthesis is a route-selection and falsification tool, not a path theorem or a solution of Erdos Problem 1041.
